items.title: Overview
items.description: FHIR Server integration for Health Assistant, the self-hosted, open-source health records platform. Two-way sync with an external FHIR R4 server — a hospital (Epic/Cerner), a personal health record, or a local HAPI — pulling the full patient record in and pushing observations back out.

items.title: Authorization & Connection
items.description: Connect a FHIR server to Health Assistant. SMART-on-FHIR standalone launch with Dynamic Client Registration for hospitals, or tokenless mode for a local HAPI server. Scopes, the Authorize flow, and the Check Connection action.

items.title: Pull (Full Patient Record)
items.description: Multi-resource pull from a FHIR server into Health Assistant. Ingest observations, conditions, encounters, documents, medications, allergies, and immunizations through the canonical write services with per-resource cursors and dedup.

items.title: Push (Outbound Observations)
items.description: Push local Health Assistant observations back to a FHIR server via conditional update. Idempotent per local UUID, subject rewriting, echo exclusion, best-effort Provenance, and insufficient-scope detection.

items.title: Selecting the Remote Patient
items.description: How Health Assistant maps a local patient to a remote FHIR patient. The Find Patient picker with MRN auto-suggest, manual remote patient ID entry, and the SMART launch-token fallback.

items.title: Catalog Proposals
items.description: Human-in-the-loop biomarker proposals from a FHIR server. Unmapped LOINC and SNOMED codes observed remotely queue for review; approving one defines the biomarker so future pulls map cleanly. AI proposes, you approve.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.description: Diagnose a FHIR server integration in Health Assistant. Resolve a stuck PENDING status, insufficient-scope write errors, 401 token races, empty pulls, and connection failures against HAPI or SMART endpoints.
